mistakes.why: Half of 4 is 2: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + 4x + 5</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (x + 2)^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

The top would have to be <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x + 4</annotation></semantics></math> for the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math> form. With 1 on top, complete the square.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{1}{x^2 + 9}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x^2 + 9}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{1}{9}\cdot\frac{1}{(x/3)^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>; with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = \frac{x}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dx = 3\,du</annotation></semantics></math>, which leaves <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{9}</annotation></semantics></math> is offset by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dx = 3\,du</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which integral is best started by completing the square?

Divide the top by <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math> first, then evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \frac{x^3 + x + 1}{x^2 + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \frac{1}{x^2 + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \arctan 1</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>. The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math> form needs <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x</annotation></semantics></math> on top.

The remainder term <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math> adds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{\pi}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{x^3 - 1}{x - 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x \ne 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{1}{x^2 + 8x + 20}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

Why is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2</annotation></semantics></math> put in the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> column rather than <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{2x}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: Because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{2x}</annotation></semantics></math> has no derivative that can be written down
Because the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> column is for the factor with the larger value
Either choice gives the answer in exactly three rows

Its derivatives reach 0, while <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^{2x}</annotation></semantics></math> can be integrated again and again

items.q: Which product is the second term of the answer?

Use the table to find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int x^2 e^{2x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The signs must alternate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+, -, +</annotation></semantics></math>: the middle term is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2x \cdot \frac{1}{4}e^{2x} = -\frac{x}{2}e^{2x}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is only the first diagonal. Keep going until the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> column reaches 0: three diagonals, three terms.

The last diagonal, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+2 \cdot \frac{1}{8}e^{2x} = \frac{1}{4}e^{2x}</annotation></semantics></math>, is missing. Stop only when the <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math> column reaches 0.

items.q: Find the value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 x^2 e^{2x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math> the antiderivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">e^0\left(0 - 0 + \frac{1}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, not 0. Subtract it.

The signs did not alternate: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math>. The middle term is subtracted: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The same method is used for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int x^3 \sin x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>, with <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x^3</annotation></semantics></math>. How many terms does the answer have?
options: It goes on forever, because <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin x</annotation></semantics></math> keeps cycling

items.q: To evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^4 x f'(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> by parts, which choice works?
options: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dv = f'(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">du = dx</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v = f''(x)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = xf(x)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dv = dx</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">du = f(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v = x</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dv = f'(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">du = dx</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v = f(x)</annotation></semantics></math>

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = f'(x)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dv = x\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">″</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">du = f''(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v = \frac{x^2}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Find the value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^4 x f'(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msubsup><mo stretchy="true" symmetric="true" minsize="1.8em" maxsize="1.8em">|</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>17</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">xf(x)\Big|_1^4 = 20 - 3 = 17</annotation></semantics></math> is only <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>v</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">uv</annotation></semantics></math>. Subtract <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^4 f(x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 6</annotation></semantics></math>.

Integration by parts subtracts the new integral: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mi>v</mi><mo>−</mo><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>v</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">uv - \int v\,du</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>17</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17 - 6</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>17</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17 + 6</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> is the left side at <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = -3</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{2}{x - 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2\ln|x - 1|</annotation></semantics></math>: keep the coefficient <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_2^4 \frac{x + 7}{(x - 1)(x + 3)}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

Subtracting it adds <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

The piece <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{x + 3}</annotation></semantics></math> integrates to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\ln|x + 3|</annotation></semantics></math>; with a plus sign the value changes to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mn>63</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln\frac{63}{5}</annotation></semantics></math>.

At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 1</annotation></semantics></math> the antiderivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\ln 1 - 3\ln 3 = -3\ln 3</annotation></semantics></math>, not 0; subtract it.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^\infty \frac{dx}{x^2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1 - 0</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1</annotation></semantics></math> since the curve approaches 0

Which integral should start with polynomial long division?

Evaluate integral III, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{1}{x^2 + 2x + 2}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math> form needs the bottom's derivative, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x + 2</annotation></semantics></math>, on top. With 1 on top, complete the square: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x + 1)^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

Half of 2 is 1: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + 2x + 2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= (x + 1)^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Evaluate integral IV, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{x^2 + 1}{x - 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The remainder is 2: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x - 1)(x + 1) = x^2 - 1</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^2 + 1 - (x^2 - 1) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

The quotient is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 1</annotation></semantics></math>: check by multiplying, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x - 1)(x + 1) + 2</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= x^2 + 1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find the correct value of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mn>1</mn></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^1 \frac{6x}{x^2 + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6x\,dx = 3\,du</annotation></semantics></math>; the factor is 3, not 6.

The arctan form is for a constant on top. Here the top is a multiple of the bottom's derivative: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which check confirms that <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\ln(x^2 + 1)</annotation></semantics></math> is an antiderivative of <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6x}{x^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>?
options: Its graph looks like a parabola near 0

items.q: Another student writes <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{6x}{x^2 + 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>arctan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 6\arctan x + C</annotation></semantics></math>. What is the reason this is wrong?
options: The answer should have <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mn>6</mn><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ 6C</annotation></semantics></math>

The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> in the numerator: arctan fits <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{x^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{x}{x^2 + 1}</annotation></semantics></math>

Arctan needs <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{1 - x^2}</annotation></semantics></math> on the bottom

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{1}{1 + 4x^2}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \sec^2(3x)\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Its derivative is <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3\sec^2(3x)</annotation></semantics></math>. Divide by the 3 from the inside.

The power rule does not apply to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sec^2</annotation></semantics></math>; read <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfrac><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>sec</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>⋅</mo><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0">′</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dx}\tan u = \sec^2 u \cdot u'</annotation></semantics></math> backward.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msqrt><mi>x</mi></msqrt></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int \frac{x + 1}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The top and the bottom cannot be integrated separately. Split first: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{1/2} + x^{-1/2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int x^{-1/2}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{x^{1/2}}{1/2}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2x^{1/2}</annotation></semantics></math>: the power goes up to <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Find <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mi>x</mi><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msqrt><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int x\sqrt{x - 1}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math> for <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 1</annotation></semantics></math>, using <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x - 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Include <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">+</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+ C</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> outside cannot be treated as a constant. With <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u = x - 1</annotation></semantics></math>, write <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = u + 1</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>u</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int (u + 1)u^{1/2}\,du</annotation></semantics></math>.

An integral of a product is not the product of the integrals. Rewrite <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = u + 1</annotation></semantics></math> and expand.

items.q: Pick a method and evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>0</mn><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mfrac><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_0^{\ln 2} \frac{e^x}{1 + e^x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: At <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 + e^0 = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, so subtract <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln 2</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ln 3 - \ln 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

That evaluates the integrand-like expression <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{1 + e^x}</annotation></semantics></math>. items.q: Choose a substitution and evaluate <math class="calc-m"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mo largeop="true" movablelimits="false">∫</mo><mn>1</mn><mi>e</mi></msubsup><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ln</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><mi>x</mi></mfrac><mspace width="0.1667em"></mspace><mi>d</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_1^{e} \frac{1 + \ln x}{x}\,dx</annotation></semantics></math>.
